what: The Unreal look's own settings, read by the probe at run time (ue-probe/Source/LedgerProbe/Public/StreetMeshes.h ParseLook) so that tuning the frame against the Hook sheet is a file edit and a frame, not a build. Jafar, 23 September: the look is developed in Unreal against the sheet, in one pass. A missing file or key keeps the constant the probe always used, and the verdict line says lookFrom and lookRead.
sky_seen_gain_note: The sky dome as SEEN, over the sky intensity that lights the street: the sheet's sky is white over a dark street. Tuned 23 September against the sheet at the approved lens with the probe's own frame measured by region; 1.0 was the probe's constant.
street_glow_gain_note: Blender's glow strengths (tubes 12, lit rooms 3.4 by day and 0.7 at night) into this engine's unitless emissive. 0.10 was the first value.
wet_film_from_note: From this wetness the road, the paving and the kerb lose their relief map: the pack's relief is strong and scattered every reflection a wet road shows (23 September, found by rendering the road without it: it mirrored the facades and the sky as the sheet's does). The day is 0.6 and the night 0.9, so both are films of water; 2.0 would mean never.
picture_room_gain_note: How much brighter a pictured shop room reads than the light on the facade, standing in for Blender's glow.
glass_see_through_note: The display glass wears M_LedgerGlass (tools/ue/make_glass_material.py): translucent, lit in the forward pass so the sky lands on it as a sheen, tinted by the glass colour. If the build lacks that material the glass is left out, as it was before it existed; the verdict line counts both.
sun_gain_note: The Unreal day's sun is this times the scene file's sun_intensity. The sheet is overcast with no sun shadow; at the file's 3.0 the parade threw a hard shadow across the road.
sky_light_gain_note: The sky light on the street is this times the scene file's sky_intensity, so the seen sky can be bright while the walls stay as dark as the sheet's.
surface_gain_note: Per-surface colour in this engine, by base material, over the drawn surface's own colour. Retuned 23 September again once the drawn bricks and flags carry Blender's wear (patches, the splash at the foot, streaks from the wall head, about 0.6 of the clean wall on average): brick_red lands the parade's upper wall at 78/46/33 against the sheet's 76/45/35; paving at 126/112/98 against the sheet's wet 122/106/87; interior_lit is the flat back wall and the pictured rooms (their own gain is picture_room_gain).
night_note: The three day gains are the day's only. The night's own, tuned 23 September by eye for the roadmap's dusk frame (the street at dusk, wet, lamps lit, a figure in silhouette) - there is no night reference sheet: the night sky photograph at 0.15 of its brightness, so the terraces stand dark against an evening sky instead of a white one, the sky light as the file has it, and the automatic exposure biased down one stop.
wet_floor_note: 23 September, after two tries in Unreal and the recipe's own two in Blender: the flags take the recipe's wet roughness and no floor of their own. 0.25 mirrored the sky and read 1.6-2.5x the sheet and blue; 0.40 still 1.05/1.15/1.37. The sheet's shine is the shopfront reflected close to the wall, which a lower roughness does not give. SET ASIDE. The paving gain cooled to 0.72/0.56/0.30 instead: the near footway 1.04/1.04/1.17 of the sheet.
street_in_play_note: The Blender street is shown in the playable game too - the walk, the crime, a plain launch - in place of the scene file's own terrace, ground and sign pieces, which are hidden and keep their collision, so walking, blocking and every sight line behave exactly as before. The Blender street's own collision is a later step.
fog_note: THE FAR END'S DEPTH, tuned 23 September against the sheet with the street's new bend and hillside: the day's fog allowed three times the scene file's cap (0.100 -> 0.300; the file's number is in the names of its fog-series rows and was ruled for another street), and a light fog colour, since at the day's exposure the old 0.55 grey read as a darkening. The far end measures 120/109/101 against the sheet's 120/108/104.
night_exposure_pin_note: 23 September. A night row that asks the scene file for no exposure pin is held here instead of left automatic: the lit rooms seen through the see-through glass throw the automatic meter, and cam_A beside Mickey's window came out black (mean 0.0 on three local takes, and on the runner in two runs of four). 0.1 is where a healthy dusk frame's automatic exposure already settles: the hook camera's dusk measured 22.1 automatic and 22.8 held at 0.1, locally. Rows with their own pin keep it.
